name: IGF-1 LR3
used_for: IGF-1 LR3 is a lab-made analog of insulin-like growth factor 1 with an arginine substitution and an N-terminal extension, which lowers its binding to IGF-binding proteins. It is sold online as a research chemical for muscle growth, and sources describe it as never approved or evaluated in a human clinical trial. The only approved IGF-1 analog is mecasermin (Increlex), which is a different molecule indicated for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency in children. Evidence on LR3 itself is limited to animal and laboratory work, and it is prohibited in sport.

administration_guidance.text: The approved IGF-1 analog mecasermin (Increlex, a different molecule from LR3) is administered by subcutaneous injection only, with injection sites rotated, and the label says to give it shortly before or after (within 20 minutes of) a meal or snack because of its insulin-like hypoglycemic effects.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Increlex label says unopened vials are refrigerated at 2 to 8 C and not frozen, protected from light, and that an opened vial is kept refrigerated and used within 30 days. This is label storage for mecasermin, not for IGF-1 LR3.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: HubMed Ed, an education company that promotes its own peptide-therapy courses and does not sell IGF-1 LR3, says it is given by subcutaneous injection into the abdomen or thigh and that taking it with some carbohydrates can help keep blood sugar stable. It says the peptide stays active for 20 to 30 hours.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The Increlex (mecasermin) label warns of severe hypoglycemia including seizures, intracranial hypertension, tonsil and adenoid enlargement, slipped capital femoral epiphysis and scoliosis progression, and contraindicates it in children with active or past malignancy. LR3 itself has no human label.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Peptide Protocol Wiki, an educational site that says it does not sell products, lists oncogenic potential through IGF-1 receptor signaling, severe hypoglycemia, unregulated product quality and the absence of any human clinical trial as the main risks of IGF-1 LR3.
side_effects.label: internet

side_effects.text: HubMed Ed lists blood sugar swings, hypoglycemia if injected without eating, insulin resistance with frequent use, water retention, headaches, joint stiffness and a theoretical risk of stimulating abnormal cell growth.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: A video from the channel Peptide Buddy calls itself a fact-versus-fiction review of IGF-1 LR3 and IGF-1 DES, with a reference list of PubMed papers in the description and a link to the creator's Patreon.
A bodybuilding federation video features a doctor discussing the science of IGF-1 LR3 and how it compares with growth-hormone-releasing peptides, framed as performance against risk.
A fitness channel includes IGF-1 LR3 in a peptide bulking stack alongside HGH, tesamorelin and CJC/ipamorelin for muscle building and recovery.
A supplement retailer's video calls IGF-1 LR3 the ultimate peptide for muscle growth and fat loss and links to its own article and a discount code.
The Peptide Protocol Wiki states that in the United States IGF-1 LR3 is an unregulated research reagent that is not FDA-approved, and that the World Anti-Doping Agency bans it.

research.summary: FDA prescribing information for Increlex (mecasermin), the approved recombinant IGF-1 for growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency. Included as the approved IGF-1 analog, not as a label for IGF-1 LR3.
research.finding: Documents the hypoglycemia, intracranial hypertension, lymphoid hypertrophy and malignancy warnings, meal timing and storage that apply to approved IGF-1, which gives context for the insulin-like effects of IGF-1 analogs.

research.summary: Study (Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab) of one week of IGF-1 LR3 infusion in growth-restricted fetal sheep versus vehicle.
research.finding: LR3 did not improve fetal growth, and circulating amino acids fell, which the authors suggest may reflect higher amino acid use. It is a fetal sheep study.

research.summary: Study (J Alzheimers Dis) of intranasal LR3-IGF-1 for seven months in a mouse model of Alzheimer disease, with cell experiments.
research.finding: LR3 improved body composition and altered amyloid plaque features but did not significantly change cognitive symptoms, so the authors say it does not support LR3 as a monotherapy.
